title: Port smol-toml (TypeScript, 1.6k lines) to Go, judged by toml-test
prompt: /workspace holds smol-toml, a TOML 1.0 parser and serializer in TypeScript (src/, about 1,600 lines; toml-test-parse.mjs and toml-test-encode.mjs show how it maps to toml-test's JSON). Port it to Go in /workspace/go: package toml at the module root (go.mod is given: module smoltoml, Go 1.24, standard library only, no third-party modules), with the same behaviour, plus two commands, cmd/toml-decoder and cmd/toml-encoder, that follow the toml-test protocol in PROTOCOL.md for TOML 1.0: the decoder reads TOML on stdin and prints its JSON description, or exits 1 on invalid TOML; the encoder reads a JSON description and prints TOML. Do not change the TypeScript. You have go_build and go_decode tools that build /workspace/go in a fresh container (sub-agents do not have them), so build after each round of changes. Reply with a short summary when done.

judge.command: hidden/run.sh: go build both commands with GOPROXY=off, then toml-test test -toml 1.0 -json
judge.parse: the summary line 'toml-test v… : passed N, failed M'
judge.image: judge/Dockerfile: golang:1.27.3-bookworm with toml-test v2.2.0 installed; scoring runs with --network none, 4 CPUs

source.why: A real cross-language port where the judge is the language-independent suite every TOML implementation is held to, as Bun's TS tests judged the Rust. Small enough to finish in about an hour with a dozen children.
source.reference: reference/go: BurntSushi/toml v1.6.0 (MIT, stdlib only) as module smoltoml with its toml-test commands; scores 0.989 (it rejects 449 of the 474 invalid cases)
